absent: Locking discipline and concurrency rules for these descriptors are not shown in the fragments.
State machines for Opal locking, shadow boot, revert, and attestation flows are not shown.
System call numbers, kernel handlers, and error return conventions for semaphore and shared memory operations are not shown.
Driver side effects and validation rules for socket interface, routing, bonding, bridge, and hardware timestamp controls are not shown.
Firmware wire formats for attestation reports and derived keys beyond buffer sizes are not shown.
Lifetime, ownership, and cleanup rules for pending semaphore operations and undo entries are not shown.

findings.text: User space controls self encrypting drive Opal behavior through a family of device operations sharing one magic value together with status geometry discovery and generic table descriptors.

A generic table transfer descriptor bundles caller authentication alongside an opaque data handle plus an eight element table identity plus a start location plus a length plus control bits plus private context. The header distinguishes a retrieval operation from an update operation and provides one single bit selector for each derived from its enumeration position.
Table identity holds eight octets. Retrieval selector equals one and update selector equals two, matching single bit masks for enumeration positions zero and one.

Seven capability and state indicators occupy successive single bit positions from bit zero through bit six with values doubling each step, covering general support then locking support then locking active then locked condition then shadow boot enabled then shadow boot completed then single user range support.

Device status pairs a four octet flag word with reserved space. Geometry groups a one octet alignment hint with a four octet block size and two eight octet values for granularity and lowest aligned address plus trailing pad octets. Discovery pairs a location token with a size token. Locking scope revert pairs authentication material with a four octet option selector plus pad.

Ten device controls numbered two twenty through two twenty nine share one magic and move data from caller toward kernel, covering save then lock handling then ownership then scope activation then password update then user activation then trusted area revert then range setup then user to range assignment then shadow boot toggling. Save with lock handling and user assignment use a lock descriptor, ownership with trusted revert use a key, scope activation uses a range activation descriptor, password update uses a new password descriptor, user activation uses a session descriptor, range setup uses a range setup descriptor, shadow toggling uses a boot area descriptor.

Ten further controls numbered two thirty through two thirty nine share the same magic, with device status and geometry queries returning data outward and the remainder accepting caller data. In order they request range erasure, secure range erasure, physical identity revert, shadow completion, shadow write, generic table exchange, device status, range status, geometry, and discovery. Erasures use session descriptors, physical revert uses a key, shadow completion and shadow write use their dedicated boot descriptors, table exchange uses a table descriptor, and each query uses its matching status geometry or discovery descriptor.

Seven closing controls numbered two forty through two forty six share the same magic, with six transferring a caller structure inward and one reset carrying no payload. They cover scope revert, service identity password update, scope reactivation, range start and length update, range enablement, single user range query, and stack reset. Revert uses a revert descriptor, password updates use new password descriptors, reactivation uses a reactivation descriptor, range updates share a range setup descriptor, and the single user query uses a range summary descriptor.
Security policy netlink messages form a small consecutive run beginning at sixteen, with enforcement control at the base value, policy load one higher, and an upper bound sentinel one further.

Legacy event mask defines empty as zero, access control audit as lowest bit, and all as every bit set. Multicast indices define none as zero and audit as one, with a maximum derived as one less than the closing sentinel.
Enforcement update carries a single signed four octet value. Policy load notification carries a single unsigned four octet sequence identifier.

Semaphore operation flag for automatic undo on exit equals four thousand ninety six. Seven control selectors run consecutively eleven through seventeen for reading creator process, reading one value, reading all values, counting nonzero waiters, counting zero waiters, writing one value, and writing all values in order.
Three diagnostic selectors follow at eighteen nineteen and twenty for status by index, system information, and status regardless of permission.

A semaphore set descriptor combines access permissions with last operation and last change timestamps plus internal references to the value array, pending queue front and back, and undo chain, plus a member count. One queued operation combines a two octet member index with a signed two octet adjustment plus a signed two octet flag field.

Control argument offers a choice among an integer for single value writes, a user pointer to a set descriptor for status handling, a user pointer to an array for bulk reads and writes, a user pointer to a limits block for system information, or a generic user pointer pad. The limits block holds ten integers describing map size, identifier count, total semaphores, undo counts, per set and per call ceilings, undo per process, undo element size, maximum value, and exit adjustment ceiling.

System ceilings set identifier count and per identifier size each at thirty two thousand, total semaphores as their product, operations per call at five hundred, and both maximum value and exit adjustment ceiling at thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty seven.
Undo related ceilings reuse earlier values, with per process undo matching operations per call, system undo count and map size matching total semaphores, and undo element footprint fixed at twenty.

Attestation request carries sixty four octets of caller data plus a privilege level plus reserved pad. Attestation response provides four thousand octets of opaque firmware output. Key derivation request groups root selector with reserved space plus an eight octet field selector plus privilege level plus guest version plus an eight octet platform version. Key derivation response provides sixty four octets of opaque output.

Guest request envelope starts with a one octet message version that must be nonzero, followed by two eight octet location tokens for input and output, followed by an eight octet combined error word viewable either whole or as low firmware code plus high manager code. Extended report request embeds a full attestation request plus an eight octet certificate location plus a four octet certificate length. All three guest controls share magic letter S.
Three bidirectional controls numbered zero one and two retrieve an attestation report, derive a key, and retrieve an extended report with certificates, each exchanging the common guest envelope.

Combined error keeps firmware status in the low thirty two bits and manager status shifted up by thirty two, with helpers to isolate each half and to combine them. Manager codes define invalid length as one and busy as two.

Shared memory sizing sets smallest segment at one octet and system wide identifier count at four thousand ninety six. Largest single segment in octets and system wide total in pages share one ceiling computed as the unsigned long maximum minus sixteen megabytes. Per process attachment ceiling equals system identifier count.

A shared segment descriptor combines permissions with a four octet size plus three timestamps for last attach detach and change plus creator and last operator identifiers plus a current attachment count plus compatibility and unused pointer slots.
Classic access bits use octal four hundred for read and two hundred for write. Creation modifiers use octal four thousand for huge page backing and octal ten thousand for skipping reservation checks.

Huge page size selection reuses generic huge flag shift and mask encodings and offers named sizes from sixty four kilobytes through sixteen gigabytes including half megabyte, one, two, eight, sixteen and thirty two megabyte, plus two fifty six and five twelve megabyte and one, two and sixteen gigabyte steps.

Attach modifiers use octal ten thousand for read only, twenty thousand for address rounding, forty thousand for replacement mapping, and one hundred thousand for execute access. Locking selectors are eleven for lock and twelve for unlock. Diagnostic selectors are thirteen for status, fourteen for info, and fifteen for unrestricted status.

Static limits block holds five integers for maximum and minimum segment, identifier count, per process ceiling, and system total. Runtime usage block reports active identifier count plus unsigned totals for allocated, resident and swapped memory plus counters for swap attempts and successes.
Socket diagnostics query header pairs a one octet address family with a one octet protocol selector.
Two diagnostics operations exist, one numbered twenty for dumping sockets by family and one numbered twenty one for requesting destruction.

Socket memory accounting defines nine ordered counters for receive allocation, receive buffer, transmit allocation, transmit buffer, forward allocation, queued transmit, option memory, backlog, and drops, followed by a count sentinel.
Diagnostics multicast enumerates none then four destroy notification groups for version four and six transport pairs, with a maximum defined as one less than the closing sentinel.

Storage introspection defines three small enumerations each starting at none with a maximum one less than its sentinel, covering request map descriptor selection, reply container selection, and inner attributes for pad, map identity and map value.

Generic address storage reserves one hundred twenty eight octets overall, shaped as a choice between an alignment pointer and a family field followed by filler sized to fill the remainder. Family uses an unsigned two octet integer.
Buffer pinning uses bit zero for transmit size and bit one for receive size with a combined mask of both. Transmit hash policy uses two fifty five for default, zero for disabled, and one for enabled.

Queue level queries reuse generic unread and unsent size primitives. Socket control family is hex eighty nine. New stamp queries use subcodes six and seven to return paired eight octet time values, while portable aliases choose between legacy and new encodings according to native time object width or configuration.

Routing table controls occupy three consecutive codes beginning at hex eighty nine zero B for add, remove and an unused slot. Interface management spans hex eighty nine ten through hex eighty nine forty three with single code gaps after hardware retrieval and after device count, covering in numeric order naming lookup, link setting, listing, flag get and set, protocol address get and set, peer address get and set, broadcast address get and set, mask get and set, metric get and set, memory get and set, unit size get and set, name setting, hardware setting, encapsulation get and set, hardware retrieval, subordinate get and set, multicast add and drop, index lookup with alias, extended flag set and get, address deletion, broadcast hardware, device count, bridge get and set, and queue length get and set.

Device tooling uses hex eighty nine forty six for generic tool access, forty seven through forty nine for physical layer address and register get and set, four A for wide area parameters, four B for unsent only queue size, and four C for network namespace retrieval. Address resolution uses fifty three through fifty five for delete get set and sixty through sixty two for reverse delete get set. Device parameter get and set use seventy and seventy one. Link and virtual lan controls use eighty through eighty three for link add delete and lan get set.

Bonding controls run hex eighty nine ninety through ninety five for enslaving, release, hardware update, subordinate query, bond query, and active change. Bridging uses A zero through A three for bridge add delete and port add delete. Hardware stamping uses B zero for set and get combined and B one for get only. Device private block begins at F zero covering through F F and protocol private begins at E zero covering through E F.
Type mask is 00170000 octal. Type values are 0140000 for socket, 0120000 for link, 0100000 for regular, 0060000 for block, 0040000 for directory, 0020000 for character, and 0010000 for fifo.
Privilege bits are 0004000 for set user, 0002000 for set group, and 0001000 for sticky.
Link test masks a mode with the type mask and compares against the link code, yielding true only for symbolic links.

Several maxima derive as one less than a closing sentinel rather than as independent values, including multicast group limits and storage selector limits. Combined masks equal bitwise union of member bits, including buffer lock combination and error word composition from low and high halves.

Reserved and pad fields accompany variable or aligned structures and must remain zero or ignored, including attestation pad, key derivation reserved word, status reserved word, geometry pad, revert pad, and address storage filler whose length equals total reservation minus family size. Product and alias relations hold among limits such as total semaphores equaling identifier count times per identifier size and per process segment ceiling equaling system count.

Several descriptors carry raw user location tokens plus lengths that the kernel must validate before dereference, including table data handles, discovery and certificate locations with byte counts, attestation output buffers, control choices with embedded user pointers, and interface queries returning variable length lists. Timestamp selection depends on native type width, so mismatched builds choose different encodings.
One reply limit macro uses DIAB in its middle letters where sibling macros use DIAG, and implementations must preserve the observed spelling for compatibility.
